title: Meetings on the Move
passage:
Ask a group of office workers to describe their most {{1}} meetings and few will mention a conference room. The ones they remember tend to be conversations that happened while moving: on a walk to a nearby cafe or around a city block. That observation has led some managers to {{2}} the traditional seated discussion with a walking meeting, in which colleagues talk side by side rather than facing each other across a table.

Supporters insist the change is more than a fashion. Walking gives the body a steady rhythm, and that rhythm appears to {{3}} the grip of the usual workplace routine. Ideas that might have been ignored are more likely to be voiced. Because nobody is typing, the exchange becomes more {{4}}: people listen, pause, and answer in full sentences instead of firing off quick replies.

The arrangement also shifts the balance of power. In a conference room whoever sits at the head of the table tends to dominate, but outdoors that hierarchy {{5}}. Quieter members find it easier to {{6}} to the discussion, and a junior employee may speak as freely as a director. Difficult news, some say, is delivered more honestly on a footpath.

The method is not suitable for everything. A {{7}} budget needs a spreadsheet, and a complex plan needs diagrams that nobody can {{8}} while crossing a street. Weather is another {{9}} consideration, and long routes may leave out colleagues with {{10}} mobility. Experienced organisers therefore keep walks short, choose flat paths, and reserve the format for informal thinking. Used with care, a walk can turn a dull update into a conversation.

blanks.explain: 空格修饰 meetings，后文“the ones they remember”提示是“令人难忘的”，故填 memorable；hostile、fragile 与语境不符。
replace A with B 表示“用 B 取代 A”，与后面的 with a walking meeting 呼应；postpone、borrow、abandon 都不能构成该搭配。
appear to 后接动词原形，loosen the grip of... 意为“放松……的束缚”；postpone、borrow 等无法与 the grip 搭配。
because nobody is typing 以及人们认真倾听、完整作答，说明交流更“坦率”，candid 符合；hostile 与前后语气相反。
主语 hierarchy 为第三人称单数，dissolve 表示“（等级差别）消失”，语法与语义都成立；其余动词不合。
contribute to 表示“参与、对……有所贡献”；postpone、borrow 等不能接 to，abandon 语义也不合。
修饰 budget，指“详尽的预算”，需要形容词；hostile、fragile 语义不合。
sketch diagrams 意为“画示意图”，与“过马路时无法画图”的语境相符；borrow、abandon 不合。
practical consideration 指“实际层面的考虑”，天气和路线都属于实际因素；fragile 等不合。
limited mobility 是固定搭配，意为“行动不便”，与 long routes 的顾虑一致；hostile、fragile 不合。
